utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. I understand, Mr. Djurdjic, that there may be a matter you want to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would seek some clarification and it significantly affects the preparations of the Defence and the efficacy of these proceedings. The Defence has noted, especially in terms of the notification provided for the next three witnesses, that the paragraphs that are specifically mentioned in relation to the witnesses who are to be heard actually differ from those stated in the 65 ter annexes of the pre-trial brief. In actual fact, what is mentioned here are 1 through 5, and perhaps paragraphs 72, 75, and 73, for instance. There aren't any others. Whereas in the pre-trial brief, in the summary, there are other paragraphs that are referred to, especially for Gerxhaliu and Sabit Kadriu, the next two witnesses. And that has happened so far as well with crime-base witnesses. The preparations considerably differ and the duration of the cross itself if we restrict ourselves only to the crime-based paragraphs. If we have to deal with the historical context and the political part, say 85, 84, up to 90, then the way in which we have to prepare and conduct our cross becomes completely different. I would appreciate it if the OTP could explain whether these are mere omissions or are they actually revising or redacting their pre-trial brief. So what we received by way of notification is different. Let me be specific on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do I look to Ms. Nilsen?

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thank you. When it comes to the upcoming witness, Ms. Fedrije Xhafa, I'm not quite sure whether it is like my learned colleague has stated now, that it is a discrepancy between the 65 ter list and the notification that the Prosecution has already provided counsel. In the 65 ter witness list, the -- described paragraphs from the indictments are 72(m), 75(j), and 100 -- which is exactly the same as in the notification to the Defence. So I am a little unsure what he is referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps you could help there, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. In the pre-trial brief, precisely for this lady where the deviation is the smallest as it were it is --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please slow down when giving numbers, reading out numbers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Djurdjic, you've got ahead of the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. I'll take it slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Whenever we get excited we get fast. We need to slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I forget that there is interpretation of what I am saying. For Ms. Fedrije Xhafa, in the pre-trial brief the following paragraphs are mentioned 25 to 32, 72(m), 72(l), and 100. We received notification for 72(m), 75, and 77 respectively. However, let me tell you, it's not really that important for her --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Again counsel is giving numbers too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could we kindly ask Mr. Djurdjic to read out the numbers at a regular pace. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: One of the biggest problems seems to be when you're reading numbers, you slip through them very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm reading the notification for Dr. Shukri Gerxhaliu. We received on the 30th or on the 29th, I don't know exactly, the paragraphs were the following: 72(m), 75(i), and 77. In the pre-trial brief the references are the following: 16, 23 through 32, 72(m), 73, 75(j), 77, and 100. In relation to the next witness, and I don't have him over here right now, there are again significant differences between the notification and what is mentioned in the 65 ter pre-trial brief. I would just like to tell you the following: If it only has to do with the crime base, then my cross is much shorter and faster, of course and more effective and efficient; but if we prepare in line with the pre-trial brief, then it takes longer for the historical, political context and the first part that has to do with joint criminal enterprise, or rather -- rather, paragraphs from 28 to 32. That is why I don't understand. If the OTP is reducing these witnesses that they're calling now only to the crime base, if they are changing the summary of the pre-trial brief, then could we please be told as much and then we are going to prepare in line with that and then we'll be faster and more efficient. Let us know what the subject of the testimony is. Oh, I see, I am sorry, Mr. Stamp has arrived. Yes. I see that now, so he will be able ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Nilsen or Mr. Stamp? We will -- whoever would like to have the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, I really wish to be economical on time, and I'm afraid that I do not follow fully what the complaint is. It seems to me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The complaint is that in the pre-trial brief you have given references to a number of paragraphs or passages in the indictment to which the witness is said by the Prosecution to be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: In the witness notifications that have been given in the last week or two, two weeks ahead of the witness coming, the references to the indictment, in some cases at least, are much shorter and do not include some of the references that were originally given. Now, the Defence, not unreasonably, wants to know is this a conscious and deliberate narrowing of the scope of the evidence of the witness so that the Prosecution will not rely on this witness in the case in respect of the wider range of references to the indictment originally suggested? Or is it that for some other reason you simply shortened the references to the indictment? Is this something you're able to deal with at this moment or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I was about to indicate that I would prefer to deal with it at the next break. I can say in respect to the next witness, the notification in the filed summaries, 65 ter summaries, is the governing notification even if -- and I'm not sure if it applies to this witness, even if in that case, the case of the next, upcoming witness, the filed notification of two days ago refers only to the crime base. The governing notification is the 65 ter unless a formal application to amend is made.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, you're going to have to help me understand what you're saying there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you saying that you are going to rely on this witness, the next one --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- only for crime base?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're saying that the original wider notification is the one that you want to provide?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I assume it is wider, that is why I am so vague because I have not been able to look at the 65 ter. Perhaps if I am told these things that these matters will be raised before, I could look at it and provide precise answers. Assuming that counsel is right and that the 65 ter filed formally is wider than the wider -- 65 ter that was formally filed governs the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, can we ask that you will look at the other witnesses and be in a position to let Mr. Djurdjic know promptly in the course of today --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: By the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- the position in respect to the coming witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. For the next witness, Mr. Djurdjic, you need to assume that it's the wider reference, and Mr. Stamp will speak to you when he's had a chance to check for the further witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. There's just something I wished to say in relation to this other witness, after the one ho is supposed to be heard now. He starts to testify from 1800 something until 1998. The Defence wanted to deal with 1800 something in a different way and to start only from 1998 to admit into evidence his statement only starting with 1998. If we start with the 1800s, as Dr. Sabit Kadriu says, I think that this is really going to last a long time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, are you able to speak about the witness of -- Dr. Kadriu and whether you really are relying on his evidence going back to the century before last?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, these are matters of background. You know, I think that aspect of the testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have the first battle of Sarajevo shortly introduced into the case, which is 1300 and I think 89 or something like that. I don't think it's going to be of a great deal of use to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Can I -- this is not the next witness, this is one of -- it's the next one for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, we might get through two or three witnesses a day if we're dealing with crime base, you see.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Indeed, indeed. But there is some background information which I think is brief, but it is probably necessary for complete understanding of some of the allegations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, you'll look into that as well as the other forthcoming witnesses and inform Mr. Djurdjic during the next break.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you then. Perhaps we could have the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card that is given to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sit down. Ms. Nilsen has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Before I start questioning the witness, I am seeking to make use of a map that has not been yet admitted into evidence, and I would ask your permission to use this today and add it into our 65 ter exhibit list. I can indicate the map has 65 ter number 05244 and this map was disclosed to the Defence counsel last week. I have also consulted my learned friend, and he hasn't opposed against it. And this map is quite detailed and I guess it would be to our benefit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Ms. Xhafa, could you please state your full name and birth date.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: My name is Fedrije Xhafa. I was born in 1964.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And where are you from originally?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I was born in the village of Bari, Mitrovica municipality, and now I live in the village of Maze e Ulet, Vushtrri municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: This village, Maze e Ulet, did it have another name before the war?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, it was called Saracak i Ulet.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: If it's fine with you, Ms. Xhafa, we will use this name further on in this testimony just to make it easier according to the map so far. I would like you to tell the Court what kind of occupation you had before the war in 1999.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Before the war for a short time I worked as a dress-maker. I finished a course in dress-making. After the war, in 2000, I got an employment with the police academy in Vushtrri.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I will go back to your village in Vushtrri. Where there other ethnic groups in this village than Kosovo Albanians when you lived there back in -- before the war in 1999?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, there were. There were several Serbian households.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And how many households approximately would you say was there before the war?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: About ten I would say, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Ten households all together in this village?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, but I'm not quite sure. This is what I think the number was.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Ms. Xhafa, did you testify at Milutinovic et al. trial on the 25th and the 28th of August, 2006?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And right before you testified, did you also, on the 25th of August, 2006, give your last statement to the Office of the Prosecution of this Tribunal; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you had a chance to read through your statement as well as your testimony from that trial previously before you came to witness -- to court today?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Are you referring to the last statement?

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I'm referring to both the statement that you gave back in 2006 and also the transcript from the testimony that you gave in the Milutinovic et al. case. Did you have a chance to read through those?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And as I understand there are a couple of things that you would like to amend from this statement or clarify.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: If we could have up the 65 ter number 02274. That will be the statement of 25th of August, and if we can both have the Albanian and the English version. If we could put up page 2, and on paragraph 5, just zoom in that. I have also a hard copy with me for the witness if it's difficult for her to read. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: In line 5 it reads: "Around 9.00 p.m. four Serb policemen arrived." I understand that you want to amend this information of how many there were; is that correct, Ms. Xhafa? Can you see the statements on the screen? You're on paragraph 5, line 5.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Did you have any changes regarding to how many Serb policemen who arrived?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I believe I said when I gave my statement that a large group of policemen came. We saw a large number of policemen that came on the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Fine. So instead of being specific with four policemen, you would change it to a large group of policemen arrived; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And then if we could stay on the same -- thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And then if we could stay with the same 65 ter number and move on to page 3, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: On the same paragraph but line 9 this time which reads: "The paramilitaries shouted at the tractor drivers to clear the road to allow their armed vehicles to pass." Is there something here that you would like to amend as well, Ms. Xhafa?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes. I talk about the paramilitaries here. I called paramilitaries those who wore Balaclavas and gloves at the time, but I know now that they were policemen. They -- all of them had the same uniform, blue uniform. I wanted to call them policemen in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Could you just please try to explain the reason why you then -- back then said it was the paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: At the time, I thought that those who wore Balaclavas and gloves were paramilitaries. Now that I work in a police academy, I can tell what the police uniform is and looks like those at the time who were wearing Balaclavas and gloves wore the same police uniform, the blue police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And the last thing I have noted is on e-court page 4, paragraph 9, where your 13th sentence reads: "After a while, the Serbs returned ..." Is there something that you would like to clarify regarding this matter as well? There is a sentence in the end of paragraph 9. Maybe it's difficult for you to read, but initially it says: "After a while, the Serbs returned ..." Is there anything that you would like to amend or clarify regarding this?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Yes. If you cannot read it, Ms. Xhafa, maybe you can anyway tell me is there any changes now when I'm reading it for you so that you can orally tell me if there is anything that you have -- that you want to clarify from the sentence: "After a while, the Serbs returned." Do you have something more you want or additional information who returned?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: After a while, the Serb forces returned.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And what do you mean with the "Serb forces"? Do you have any specific units that you're referring to, military, police or --

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: There were both police and military.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And did they drive in any vehicles, do you remember? If you don't remember, we can come back to it later.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Fine. Thank you, except from the last thing that you were a little bit unsure of -- with this correction now made?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know to which incident you're referring, that's why I cannot clarify. Can you please tell me which incident you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I propose that we make that clarification later when we have explained the evidence so that you can see everything in -- what happened or recall happening. Anyway, with those corrections that you have made so far, does your statement and your transcript from the Milutinovic et al. statement or trial, sorry, reflect your evidence and would you testify to the same fact today?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to seek to tender the 65 ter 05144 and 65 ter number 02274, which is respectively the transcript of Ms. Xhafa's testimony in the Milutinovic et al. case and witness statement from 25th of August, 2006. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: First the transcript will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P509, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Secondly, the statement.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- the 25th of August, 2006.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -- that will be Exhibit P510, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I would now like to provide a brief summary, Your Honours, of Ms. Xhafa's evidence. The witness describes the events leading to the convoy massacre in Studime i Eperme or Gornja Sudimlja, the 2nd of May, 1999. The witness has explained that after the NATO bombing began, the 24th of March, 1999, Serb forces started to burn the houses in the village where she and her family lived. This -- the name of this village was back then Saracak i Ulet in Albanian and Donji Svracak in Serbian. The witness's family and herself was therefore forced to leave their home, and they first went to the village Dumnica and then to Samodreza. They were here told by the KLA forces that the Serb forces were approaching and from Samodreza the witness and her family had to flee together and they went to Vesekoc where they spent five weeks. After this, they moved further to Sllakovc, where they spent two nights. They were here informed by the KLA again that the Serb forces were advancing from the north. After this, the witness and her family joined a large convoy of people moving towards Vushtrri in the municipality of Vushtrri. The witness has stated that she road a tractor together with her 13 member of family, and she has also stated how the Serb forces attacked her family several times in this convoy how her brother was shot and her father was shot and killed. The witness has also explained how her family continued on foot from Studime, where this happened, to the outskirts of Vushtrri, the town. And here they were directed into an agricultural co-operative building where the men, aged between 15 and 60 years, were separated from the rest, and how these men had to go to a prison in Smrekovnica. The witness has told how she and the rest of her family were sent to the village of Kicic after this and then to the village Dobra Luka, where the remainder of men were caught by the police and sent to the same prison in Smrekovnica. She has also described how she and all the other women had to go back to Vushtrri and obtain a written allowance from the Serb police to be able to stay in Dobra Luka. And this is the end of the witness summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Ms. Xhafa, in your statement you have described that you and your family left your home because Serb forces had begun to burn the houses in your village. Could you please explain to us which date that you left and to where you went first.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: It was the 28th of March, 1999, when they started to burn the houses in Saracak i Eperme. The population of the village began to leave. We joined the convoy, and from our village we went to Dumnice village. There we spent one night. And from there we proceeded to Samadrexha --

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: If I can stop you there, please, for a moment. When you left the 28th of March, you said that the Serb forces began to burn houses, but did you actually see this for yourself? Did you see these houses being burnt?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, one could see the flames coming out of the houses in Saracak i Eperme and the neighbours, those who lived close to the houses that were set on fire, also told me this. We all left the village and my family and I joined the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Were you at any time able to see or describe the people who you saw or who were doing this, who set fire on these houses?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: They were very far. We could not see them in the act of setting the houses on fire. We only saw the flames.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: All right. And then you went to Dumnica, where you spent one night, and then to Samodreza you have told. How many nights did you spend in Samodreza before you went further?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: In Samadrexha I remained only for a short while. We were informed that the Serb forces were coming in the direction of Samadrexha, and that's why we had to proceed to Vesekoc.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: So with a short while, you mean that you didn't stay over any nights there in Samodreza?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Half an hour, not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: All right. And then you approached to Vesekoc, where you stayed five weeks. Why did you leave Vesekoc after five weeks?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: We left Vesekoc on the 30th of April because we were informed that the police forces were advancing in two directions, that the front line was broken --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the name of the village where the front line was broken.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- the forces, the Serb forces, were shelling, and the order was given to us to leave the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: In which town did you say you were informed that the forces were broken and therefore had to leave?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: In Melenice village.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And this is in Mitrovica, right?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: It belongs to the Shala area, this village.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Fine. When you were in Vesekoc, were you aware of whether any Serb forces had taken up positions in the area around; and in that case, where?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I don't know where the Serb forces had taken up positions, but someone informed my family and the others that were there, the civilians, and told us to withdraw from that area because the Serb forces were advancing in our direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And then after you had spent approximately five weeks in Vesekoc, you went to Sllakovc. How many days or nights did you spend there?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: We stayed for two days in Sllakovc.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And why did you decide to leave from here after two days?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: For the same reason. We again heard that the Serb forces were advancing in the direction of the area where the civilians where, in Sllakovc village, and therefore we decided to join the convoy and head towards Vushtrri.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And which date are we talking about now when you decided to join the convoy and left Sllakovc?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: 2nd of May, 1999. It was about 1.00 p.m.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Were you told by anyone to join this convoy?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: People decided to form this convoy. There was nowhere for us to go. We were surrounded from all sides. The only way out, we thought, was road to Studime continuing towards Vushtrri.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And how many people would you estimate were in this convoy?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: It was a very long convoy. I cannot give you the accurate number of people, but I would say there were about 50.000 people in the convoy.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And which ethnicity did these people, this approximately 50.000 people, belong to?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: We were all Albanians, civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. We are now at the 2nd of May. You have left Sllakovc and joined the convoy towards Vushtrri. Could you please explain to the Court what happened to your family this day.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: On this day, we were ordered to stop between the two Studime villages, Studime i Eperme and Studime i Ulet. We stopped there. We sat in a field in Studime area. We were told that we could not continue to Vushtrri in the afternoon because of the curfew. They said that it was impossible to continue to Vushtrri after 4.00 p.m. because of the curfew. We stayed in this field until 9.00 p.m.; at around that time, the police forces came. They fired gun-shots in the air. They ordered the drivers to get on the tractors and make way for their forces.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: We know from your statement, Ms. Xhafa, that during this day you were approached several times, your family, by Serb forces. Could you explain this further, please.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes. My elder brother Fazli and Mirsad started to walk, whereas we, the others, went to fetch the tractor and continue on the tractor. When we arrived there after a short while, a group of policemen came. My brother Jetish and my brother's son Ismet were on the tractor. The policemen came there and asked for identification document. They began to beat Ismet and they asked for money. My brother Jetish gave them 200 Deutschemarks.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Did they explain to you why they wanted money before they released him? Did they accuse him for anything?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes. They said, Give us money or else we will kill Ismet. We gave them what we had, 200 Deutschemarks. They released Ismet. He left the tractor and came to the trailer where we were. We covered him with mattresses. After some time, I don't know when exactly, but another group of policemen came, four policemen, one of them was --

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: If I could stop you there for a moment, sorry, Ms. Xhafa. Just before you go ahead to the second group, you have described that these people were policemen. But could you describe them a little bit further. Could you give a more detailed description of how they looked, where they were, and what they looked like.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: They had blue camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And is it on this basis that you were sure that they were policemen or what?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: They also had weapons on them.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: They also had weapons. Could you see the weapons, which kind of weapons they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I don't remember what kind of weapons they had, but they did have weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Did they have any vehicles they were driving?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: No, this group didn't. This group was on foot.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: All right. And after Ismet was released and you had -- and your brother had paid them 200 Deutschemarks, did you do anything with Ismet after this event to prevent anything like that should happen again or -- explain that.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes. We placed Ismet on the trailer, covered him with mattresses. We sat around him so he couldn't be seen. He was covered in the trailer.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And before I interrupted you, you were about to explain to us about the second group. Can you please go on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: The second group came, a group of four or more policemen that were nearby. Perhaps there were more in the vicinity, but four policemen came to the place where we were. He started to beat him with a thick wooden stick on both his shoulders. My father begged them to release him. They spoke in Serbian. My father came back and told us that they again asked for money, otherwise they were going to kill Jetish. We didn't have money. At that stage, my sister-in-law Hamide gave them all her golden jewellery.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Could you please describe this person that you said was beating Jetish with this wooden stick.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: They were all dressed in blue camouflage uniforms with the exception of the person who was beating Jetish. He also wore a blue camouflage uniforms but he had a flak jacket, a green camouflage flak jacket.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And did you -- do you remember anything else about this man, how he looked, could you describe that in that case?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I remember him. He was tall. He was -- he had this wooden stick in his hands. He was blond.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. After this group of policemen had left, were you approached by several or another group after this?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes. After the first left, those who beat up Jetish, we were discussing whether to leave the tractor and walk on foot or to take the tractor. I don't know how long that lasted. Then another group came. It was a group of six policemen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And now we are talking about this third group; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the third group. Two of them were wearing masks. The four came near to the trailer and directed his arm to my mother. Then they put the weapon to Jetish's head and then they fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Did they ask for any money in advance before they did this?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: No, they didn't. This group didn't ask for any money. They simply shot Jetish. Then my father knew that it was dangerous. He went near them, said something to them, they didn't retort back. After they fired their weapon, I went to my father and wanted to make him come out of the trailer. He spoke something in Serbian. I don't know what he said. They came back and took my father with them, and then we heard the shots because I turned my head on the other side. Couldn't look at it. I heard a cry from my father. He simply cried, and then when I looked I saw that both of them were shot.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And what was the consequence of this shooting Jetish, did he survive or did he die?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: We thought that Jetish was dead, but he is still alive to this day. He escaped death.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: But you didn't know these things back then, did you?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: No. At that moment we didn't think that he was alive because he was fired at in the head, but he's still alive. But we heard of that only after a few days. We got the news that he was still alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And what about your father?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: My father died.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And after both your brother and father was shot, what did your family do next?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: They ordered us to leave that place, those policemen that were round the trailer. Ismet was the oldest of the males, but we were afraid they would shoot him so it was Lavdim who was 13 years old, my brother's son, and I asked him to drive the tractor. But he was very scared, and he didn't know how to drive the tractor. A policeman came by, came close, and he beat him with the butt of his gun, ordering him to drive on. Another policeman who was close by said to him in Albanian -- started to teach him in Albanian how to drive the tractor, and then he started using the first gear. We drove for some 100 metres or so.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: What would you estimate the time to be approximately now, Ms. Xhafa, when you stopped the tractor?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I think it must have been 11.00 --

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: In the evening --

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: -- I am not sure -- at night. I can't be precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And we know that -- from your statement, that you eventually decided to send Ismet away to inform KLA about the events. Could you please tell the Court about this.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes. At that moment we decided to quit the tractor and to continue on foot. All of us descended from the tractor. Ismet was with us and then we went on walking, trying to hide behind tractors, until we joined a group of people. The crowd was at the entrance of Studime i Ulet. We joined these people, as I said. On the way until we reached this group of people, we passed over dead bodies. We saw also my cousin Veli Xhafa. We saw he was killed on the tractor. Then we passed by some other corpses, all people lying on the floor. We saw a young guy who was injured and he was asking for help but we were scared to go and administer some help to him. Then on the way we saw a very young boy. I don't know whether he came from a tractor or so that he wanted to join us; but at that moment he was shot by the police, and I saw that he was frozen in a way let's say there. We couldn't turn our heads and look what happened, but I saw that he was there. Then we joined the crowd of people. There were no police there and all the members of my family agreed that Ismet go and join the KLA. Two other people joined Ismet and together they crossed the street and went in the direction of a mountain.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And after you had sent Ismet away to inform the KLA units, did any other group of Serb forces approach you after this on your way to Vushtrri?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, after a while they came by a military vehicle, I don't know, combat vehicle I think. And then they stopped by and ordered us to stay there until they ordered us to go towards Vushtrri. During that time, they pushed us. They wanted us to shout, to hail, Slobo Draza KLA, during the time we were there, staying on that field.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And what would this mean, Slobo Draza?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Slobo meant Slobodan Milosevic at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And Draza?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Draza I think was the name of a former Serb gang that fought in the past. This is what Draza and his gang did. I think that was a name that they ordered us to shout out loud.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And did you do this, did you shout out loud?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, some people did because they were afraid of being shot at by the police. They shouted Slobo's and Draza's name. When they ordered them to shout KLA, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you continue your way to Vushtrri by tractor?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: No, we were walking. We joined that group of people, and then we were ordered to leave for Vushtrri. They ordered us to walk on the edge of the road, and this is what we did until we arrived in Vushtrri. Then they ordered us to go to the courtyard of an agricultural co-operative there. This is where we stayed that night. It was 2.00 in the morning when we arrived there --

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Let me stop you a moment there. So you had to leave your tractor with all your belongings behind; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And -- excuse me, then you came to this co-operative or agricultural co-operative building at night. What was the situation there like when you arrived? Could you just describe that briefly.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, it was a very large group of people there. There were elderly people, children, maybe also some injured. We could hear moans, cries, people shouting, some were thirsty. It was like a horror night for me. We stayed there until the next day.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And what happened the next day, the next morning?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: On the next morning a group of policemen came there, and they started to separate the males from their families.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And -- sorry, they separated the males from the families and the age you were told was between 15 and 60; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Yes, all the males aged 15 to 60, they were set aside on the other side of the courtyard. They came also to my family and started to take Mirsad , Jetish's son; my brother Fazli; Sami; uncle Muharrem.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And did they all have to go to the prison there and then?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: No. During that time when they were being separated, my uncle Muharrem saw our neighbour dressed in uniform. We lived in the same village, Biba. He came by and my uncle said to him what happened to us in Studime. He helped us, so he saved the males of my family from being sent to prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And this prison, I understand it's -- it was located in Smrekovnica. Where did you learn those men had to go there? Did anyone tell you that the men had to go to prison in Smrekovnica?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: When they were separating the males and tell -- asking them to get on the trucks, there was a truck there. And after a while, the truck came back to get another load of men. So we heard someone said that all these men are being taken to Smrekonica prison.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And what happened to you and your family after your uncle, Muharrem, managed to get the men released? What did you do and where did you go?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: They ordered us. There was a policeman there, the one who gave the orders. Someone in the group said that his name was Simic. He ordered us to leave. Those who didn't have a tractor, he said, Go to -- back to Smrekonica or Doberlluka village. The others who had tractors should continue their way and leave for Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: This Simic, the name of this person, could you just describe him? You said he was a Serb policeman, but what made you so sure about that?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: He had the police uniform on, the green camouflage --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- blue camouflage uniform. He was rather stout with a moustache. This is what I recall of him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Did you hear anything from others who this person was, what position he had, and his occupation?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I don't remember more than that about this man.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: But you were then sent to or you travelled to Kicic, where you were accommodated. How long did you stay there with your family?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Kiciq is the name of the village.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: At that time, we did what we were ordered to. We chose this Kiciq village. My mother was suffering from heart disease, so she got on the tractor of her brother and she left for Albania, whereas we went back to Kiciq, went to an empty house where we stayed from the 3rd of March to the 7th of March in that house, after which time the family that owned that house returned and asked us to free it. So we went to Doberlluka village, where we stayed until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: In your statement you have explained about the unit who came to your house in Dobra Luka. Can you please explain to the Court what actually happened when they came.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, it was the morning of, I think, the 15th or 16th of May. They ordered us to come out. Again, they took away the males and ordered us to go to Smrekonica, to a health clinic to get a sort of card. It was I think a kind of certificate on which it was written name, last name, date of birth, place of residence, and where we were staying.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And where did you have to go to obtain this certificate?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Smrekonica. It was what we say -- we call it a health house word for word.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And what happened to the men in your family?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: They were taken away. They were ordered to bring out of their pockets all the money they had on them, and then they were sent to prison. After a while, they released Uncle Muharrem, whereas the others they kept in jail. And after two weeks, they were sent to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you get any information of the reason why you had to go and register and to obtain this certificate? Did you get any reason for it?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I don't know. That was the order given to us, but I don't know the reason why.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: If I could please ask the usher to put up 65 ter -- or it's a P number now. The previous 65 ter number 02274, the witness statement. I apologise, I don't have the P number, 509. Thank you. And it will be page 8 and 9. If we can get both pages up at the same time. If we could please have this zoomed in as much as possible, especially the -- yes, the page 8. The page that we see on the left, usher, would that be number 9, it should be a -- yeah, thank you. This should be an English translation of this certificate and not the Albanian translation. Thank you. Is it possible to have the English translation on one page and the Albanian version where we have the text on the other side? Sorry if I was vague to this. So I don't need the Albanian version of the page where there is no text. Yes. Thank you. Perfect. If you can just zoom out -- zoom in this text page.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Ms. Xhafa, do you recognise the document to the left here?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Are you able to describe what this is?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: This is a kind of certificate on notification of the place we were staying and then other data, name, last name, date of birth.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Was this a certificate that was issued to you or similar?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: No. I have brought the certificate of my niece, my brother's sister. I have a similar one here. If you need, I can show you my personal one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Well, would your personal certificate look exactly like this one except for the names and the birth dates and other information, personal information?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: It is identical, only it contains my personal data.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And the name of this, is the -- can you just tell us what the name of your niece which is described here according to you.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Fetije Xhafa.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Are you able, Ms. Xhafa, to see what is written on the stamp? I know it's pretty vague, but I don't know if we can zoom it any more than this. The other side. The stamp at -- yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "Republic of Serbia" then "Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And who issued this registration card for you? Who did you obtain it from?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: There were some people who worked in that office. There were three offices that issued such cards. My card was signed by Snjezana Bogunovic, a neighbour of ours, but the order was given to us by the police to go and obtain such certificate.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And the information that we have on the card --

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: If we can just zoom out again.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Can you just briefly explain to us what it says. We have a translated version, but just for the record so that you can tell us. First of all, I would like you to tell us the date of the card if that is correct.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: First is the name and the last name, Fetije Xhafa, then the date of birth, 15th-9-78, then I think it's the name of the place where we lived before, in Svracak, then the commune or municipality, Vucitrn. Then it reads: Republic of Serbia, then here Dobra Luka, the place where we were staying, and it's a signature and the date that this certificate was issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And the date would be?

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Ms. Xhafa, you have told us about your observations when your father was shot and killed and how your brother also was shot. You have also told us that you passed other bodies on your way to Vushtrri in the convoy. Did you see anyone else being killed or shot during this period you have told us about, either before or during or after you entered the convoy?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes. On the road from the place where we left our tractor and where we joined the convoy, through this part of the journey we came across many corpses. We saw an old man who had been killed, his horses had been killed too, relative Veli was killed in a tractor, then a young man was wounded and was asking for help. Then there was another young man who wanted to join us but who was shot and we didn't dare look back to see what happened to him. So we came across many corpses.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: But did you actually see any of these executions or it was afterwards that you saw them they were wounded or dead?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: No, they had already been killed, with the exception of this young boy who wanted to join us. He was alive. We only heard the gun-shot, but we didn't look back to see what happened to him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Except from your cousin, I believe it was, who were killed on the tractor and your father, do you have -- are you able to mention any names of the people who were killed who you mention you saw were dead?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: During this part of the journey, I only knew Veli Xhafa, a relative of mine who had been killed, not the others.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. After the massacre in Studime, where you have explained to us quite detailed, did you at any time ever see or recognise any of the perpetrators again in a later stage?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: The person who beat Jetish, I saw him again on the night of the 2nd of May at the entrance to Vushtrri. Then again, I saw him on the 15th of May when they came and ordered us to get these certificates that I spoke about.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And the men in your family and the rest that you told about who were imprisoned in Smrekovnica, when were these people released, when were these men released from the prison; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: We didn't know then, but later we found out that they had been released and sent to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Did they tell you how they were treated there in the prison?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: They did tell us about what they had gone through. They told us that there was hardly any place for them to sleep. They were tortured in different ways.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think it's time for us to take our break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you propose to tender this certificate?

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I will, Your Honours. As it is already tendered as a part of the statement in P509 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: -- I'm not going to ask to tender it again, this is the last pages of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: After the break, Your Honours, I would like the witness to point out some specific villages on the map, and that will be my last questions for her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Nilsen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I have a couple questions more before I go ahead with the map. Ms. Xhafa, when you allegedly returned back to your home village after the war ended, do you remember which date this was?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: It was two weeks after Vushtrri was liberated. The NATO forces entered Kosova on the 16th of June, so we returned to our house two weeks later. Our house was burnt down, and we lived in another house nearby.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Yes, that was the next question I was going to ask you, which conditions the village was in when you returned. Was all the houses burnt down?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: All the houses were burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And you said there were both Kosovo Albanians and other ethnicities who lived in this village, or did I get you correct there?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: You're right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: So the houses from the other ethnicities was also burnt when you returned?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: The Serb houses were not -- were not burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I see my learned friend is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right now there's no point in objecting. In response to the question as to what the situation the village was, the witness said all the houses were burned; and then the next question stated: Serbian houses, Serb houses. I don't think that was right, and the witness had given the answer that she had given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But the point, Mr. Djurdjic, is that we are seeking to learn the truthful evidence of the witness. Witnesses often misunderstand questions and give answers that may not be correct, and there has to be an opportunity to be sure with that witness that the answer they've given is the correct one. The same is applied in many of your questions. Now, it can be fully appreciated that there will be times it will be important not to suggest in any way an answer to a witness and to let the witness express themselves, but on a matter like this, the answer was simply "yes." And the next question has shown that the witness misunderstood the question, by understanding the question to be limited to non-Serb houses. Thank you, Ms. Nilsen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And just one last question, Ms. Xhafa. You said that there were ten households in this village of yours. Did you then refer -- did you the refer to the Kosovo Albanian households or did you refer to all the households together, included the Serbian households?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: The village had both Albanian and Serbian households. The houses that were near my house were Serbian. There were three Serbian houses near my house. My village is quite big. The other Serb houses are further from my house.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Maybe I didn't make myself clear. I just referred to what I asked you in the very beginning of this testimony when I asked you the number of houses in the village and you replied "ten." Is this the correct total amount of houses in the village where you were from?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: No, I was referring to the ten Serbian houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And how many Kosovo Albanian houses would there be, Ms. Xhafa?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: More than Serbian households. I think there were about 80 Albanian households at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Then I would like the usher to put up the 65 ter number 05244 which is the Kosovo map of Vushtrri municipality. And if you could please zoom in on the area to the east of Vushtrri town, and which the town would be included also into this. Thank you. Are you able to zoom in a little bit further? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Ms. Xhafa, I don't know if you can see this. It's small letters, but I hope you are able to read it. What I would like you to do is this -- as you see, this is the municipality of Vushtrri.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I would like first of all if she can have a pen, please --

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Point out your place of origin, the village where you're from, and draw a circle around it and put a number 1 next to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: If it's difficult for the witness to reach the screen. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. This will be --

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I think I made a mistake. I didn't see it very well. It should be this one.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: That's fine. And that will be the village that was formerly called Saracak i Ulet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Perhaps the court officer can erase the first circle.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Saracak i Ulet, my village.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections, Your Honour. I got an excellent map, hard copy from the OTP, and this is precisely reflected on that map. So I suggest that we give this to the witness. It will be much easier for the witness to mark this and much easier than watching this on our screens. I think it's going to be a lot more difficult if we do it on the screens. You see this map, it's an excellent map; and I think it would be much better for the Trial Chamber, a really good map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it's what's called a military ordnance map, good detail. Ms. Nilsen, do you think use of the paper copy of the map would be better?

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't know if it would be better, but we can certainly use it if it's -- I dont' have -- the thing is, I don't have a blank unannotated map left after I gave the last one to my learned colleague. But I am also sure that the witness will be able to draw this on the screen. So far so good, so I would suggest it's up to Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honour, it's the same map like the one that's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I can just ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Carry on, Ms. Nilsen, with what you're doing. We don't have spare paper copies of the map.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's a little unfortunate that what we have on the screens is not as clear as the original, but carry on and --

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I agree with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- and let us hope that the witness can pick up the area sufficiently.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: I agree with you, it's unfortunate, but we will see if we can do our best.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Then I will ask you, Ms. Xhafa, if you could please draw a line between Saracak i Ulet, or your home village, and Dumnica, where you spent your first night after you fled from your home village. Just draw a line between these two places and circle around Dumnica, like you did with the first, and put a number 2 on Dumnica, please.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: This is my village. We started our journey here. We passed through Maxhuni neighbour, through Vijance [phoen], then passed through the Dumnica road; and we spent a night somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: In Dumnica. And then I would like you to point out Samodreza village where you have told you went afterwards spent a short while, half an hour or so before you went further. If you could draw another line and put a number 3 around Samodreza.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: The following day we continued our journey. We passed through Dumnica e Eperme, through these hills, here and proceeded to Samadrexha.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And then I would like to go on with the next place you have told us you fled to where you said you spent five weeks in Vesekoc. If you also put a line from number 3 and up to here.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: From Samadrexha we passed through Ceceli, Sllakovc. I cannot see the road --

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: If we can get the usher maybe to scroll down the map a little bit just so that it's --

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: If you cannot see Vesekoc, it's fine. You can just leave it for you and --

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: It cannot be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Then if you want to -- if you know the approximate area, you can just put the ring around because you have told us that you went from there to Sllakovc. Do you see Sllakovc?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Could you draw a line up to Sllakovc and put a ring and number 5 there.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I think I should put a 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Sorry, yes, put a 4. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: And this will be Sllakovc, right?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: We passed Sllakovc, then another village, and then we arrived in Vesekoc. But you cannot see Vesekoc on the map; it's further up.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: It's further up. Okay. So after you went from Vesekoc you went to Sllakovc, and from there you joined the convoy that you have told us about. Can you see Studime in this map?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, you can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Can you draw a line to Studime and put a circle with a 5 around that.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: After we joined the convoy, we followed a road that was close to Ceceli, and from there we arrived at Studime e Eperme. And from there, we continued our journey and stopped somewhere between the two Studimes, the Upper and Lower Studime.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: You also told us that you were informed about a place where the Serb forces had taken up positions. Could you see if you can find that. It should be according to what you said in Saracak e Eperme. Are you able to see that on the map? Maybe draw a circle around that, with a letter A around that. If you don't see, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: They were, on the hills of Saracak e Eperme on the Studime side and on the other side, they were in a neighbourhood, Llazoviq neighbourhood, which is on the road.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, from Studime you have told us that you went to the outskirts of Vushtrri. Could you please -- where you went to for one night and then the men were separated from the rest, the women. Are you able to just to draw a ring around approximately where this agricultural co-operative centre were and put a number 7 around it, I believe it will be number 7.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: We continued our journey. The agricultural co-operative facility is near Vushtrri.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And then if you could also draw a circle around the place where this prison were placed in Smrekonica and put a number -- the letter B there where you were told that the men were sent to.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you have told us that you went from the agricultural co-operative centre to Kicic - I'm not very good at pronouncing it - you went there and spent a couple of nights or some days there. Could you please draw another line from Vushtrri to Kicic, please, and just put a number 8 in that ring.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And the last line I want you to draw goes from Kicic to Dobra Luka, where you told us you spent the rest of your time until the war ended and you could return to your home town. Could you please draw another line and circle around Dobra Luka and put a number 9 in it, please.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And the place where you told us that you had to go and register when you stayed in Dobra Luka, that was in Smrekovnica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: So the very same place as the prison was established also?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this annotated map into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P511, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. NILSEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. And I have no further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Nilsen. Mr. Djurdjic, do you have cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My name is Veljko Djurdjic. I am a member of the Defence team of the accused, Vlastimir Djordjevic. Together with me today is Ms. Marie O'Leary, she is also a member of our team. And since we do not speak the same language and interpretation is produced in a variety of languages, I would like to ask you to wait for me to finish my question and then give me your answer. First of all, if you do not understand a question, please let me know and I will try to rephrase it. Secondly, I would like you to answer only about the events that you yourself were an eye-witness of, things that you have direct knowledge of, and could you please indicate when your knowledge is not first-hand. I would like to start with what you said today. And it appears to me that there are some discrepancies between what you said today and your previous statement, so I would like us to clear that up. On two occasions you spoke about leaving the tractor. You said that you -- when you left the tractor that you saw many bodies, including the body of your relative in -- on the tractor. Since this is in the transcript, could you please tell me if this is a description of the same event but you only gave -- gave it twice; is that so?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: It is the same event, and I have described it earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In the statement that you gave in 2000 and 2001, there is no mention of Veli Xhafa, your relative, or indeed of the other persons that you saw as you headed towards Donja Sudimlja on foot. Could you please explain to me, why is there this discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: It is impossible that I did not mention everything that occurred that night. I have probably mentioned it in my statement of 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Ms. Fedrije, that's in paragraph 5 through 11, including this statement, the consolidated statement that was given in 2006. It's not there. Let me make this as precise as possible. This is not about the first, second, and the third group of policemen and events that involved you on the tractor; it's when you left the tractor and when you headed towards Donja Sudimlja on foot.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Lower Studime, Studime e Ulet. I have already mentioned it in my statement of 2006 when I spoke about the event involving my cousin, but I saw that the name of my cousin was changed, Emin instead of Veli Xhafa. But I think I made the correction. It was the person of Veli Xhafa, my relative.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't find it now. Let us move on and then once we've analysed it we'll be able to pin-point it. Now, you were shown the certificate of residence. The date is the 16th of May, 1992. In this certificate, is there anything that is not true?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I have given all my personal data in an accurate manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, well that's what I wanted you to say. Your personal details are correct. The place where you had residence, Donji Svrakovci, you were a resident of Donji Svrakovci; am I right?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: The place where we lived, the place where we were staying at that time, these were the data that we provided and -- as well as other data, like the name, last name, date of birth, the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you will agree with me that all the details are correct, the details that you provided that are contained in the certificate?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: My personal data are correct, the ones we saw earlier in that certificate. All the details were accurate, were correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mrs. Fedrije, could you please explain to me why you had to leave the tractor on the road between Gornja and Donja Sudimlja.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: All those people who -- that were on the tractors thought that it was more dangerous to stay on the tractors; therefore, we all decided to get off the tractors and continue to walk on foot and join the other people. That's why we also left the tractor, our tractor, and walked on trying to hide behind tractors on the way, because there were many empty tractors on the way and everybody was walking.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Ms. Fedrije, I think that you changed your statement in the statements that you made before. The problem was that who would drive the tractor and -- because your cousin was driving the tractor, he got scared, and then you got off the tractor. And you didn't say that the other people in the column had left their tractors, quite the contrary, they went on on tractors and some of them even travelled as far as Albania in those tractors.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I'm talking about the time we were in the column in Studime. After my father was -- and my brother were shot, Ismet was in hiding. We didn't dare ask Ismet to drive the tractor. That's why his son, Lavdim, 13 years old, started to drive because the police told us to leave the place where the shooting occurred. Lavdim drove the tractor for some 100 metres I think. After that, we decided to get off the tractor and walk on foot. This is what we did until we joined a group of people who were somewhere at the entrance to Studime e Ulet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your evidence today you said that since you were in the village of Veskovce, you said, Since we were surrounded we had to leave the village. What did you mean by that, surrounded from all sides?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: When I was in Vesekovc we felt safe there because it was protected by the KLA. But after that time, when we had to leave the place, going to Velenice, we were informed that the defence line was broken in that village, in Velenice, therefore the population had to flee because the danger was coming near. We didn't want something bad to happen to us. Therefore, the population had to return back to Sllakovc.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 9 you added today the military, so not only the police but the military too. You had not mentioned the military before. Do you make a distinction, or rather, did you make a distinction between the military and the police at that time?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, I knew the people who were dressed in green uniform belonged to the army, but at that time there were also people who were using vehicles and they were also green vehicles, which I think belonged to the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, if you had seen such uniforms, would you have said that you had actually seen the army, the military?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like us to get on our screens Defence document D002-5250.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Fedrije, could you please mark the uniform that you saw on the police officers.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: It doesn't seem clear to me. Maybe you can make it a little bit bigger and the colours would be clearer. This one here?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Please go ahead, and thank you. Since you mentioned the army today, could you please mark the uniform that you saw them wearing.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: I didn't pay any attention. I know that the colour was green, but I'm not sure which camouflage colour is the one that I had in mind. I know it was green, but I'm not sure which of them they were wearing that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 9 you made a change today. You said that there was a group of policemen there -- let me just check if that's paragraph 9. And in your earlier statement - let me just find it, and I do apologise -- no, it's actually in paragraph 5, I'm sorry. So in paragraph 5 you said a large group of police officers, and in the statement, the latest consolidated statement of 2006, the exact number that you provided was four policemen. So how come there is this difference?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: It's not any change. Number 4 refers to the first group that approached our tractor. At 9.00 another group came and that was a very large group.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, Madam, this is what I'm reading. It says in your statement at around 2400 [as interpreted] hours four police officers came, so that's what I'm talking about. And today you say a large group of policemen came.

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: At 2100 there was a very large group of policemen who came and ordered us to get on the tractor. Then when we were on the tractor, another group of four policemen approached our tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how far were the other policemen from that group of four men who were next to you?

utterances.speaker: FEDRIJE XHAFA
utterances.text: They walked on the road. When they gave us the order to get on the tractor, that group was walking along the way. And they ordered us that all the drivers get on the tractors. And everyone went to his or her tractor. We went to ours. We got on the tractor. Then came the other group of four policemen who came near our tractor. I didn't pay any attention to the other policemen, where they went, but I'm talking of the first group that came to the tractor.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to tender the previous document into evidence, the one with the uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The photograph showing samples of camouflage will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
